newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU envoy working on formula for Israel-Syria talks.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy working on formula for Israel-Syria talks.

text.p: Europe's envoy for the Middle East said on Saturday that he was working on a new proposal to bring Israel and Syria back for peace talks.
European Union envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos did not give any details, but he said his talks in Egypt were intended to "relaunch the bilateral track.

"There is not a final formula to get full security and full withdrawal. But that is the general format," Moratinos told Reuters as Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad held talks in Damascus on the Middle East peace process.

Moratinos was in Cairo after talks on Friday with Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, who accompanied Mubarak to Syria, and he is due to meet Egypt's presidential adviser Osama al-Baz. Moussa also met Saudi deputy foreign minister Mamoun Kurdi for talks on the Middle East peace process on Friday.

Syria's Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara toured several Arab countries, including Egypt and Saudi Arabia, over the past month to garner support for Damascus in its deadlocked talks with Israel.

Talks between Syria and Israel broke off last March when a Labour government was still in power in the Jewish state. Syria says the Labour government, which lost to Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party in elections last May, agreed to withdraw from the Golan Heights, a strategic plateau captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
Negotiations have not resumed under Netanyahu, who rejects trading occupied Arab land for peace. Syria insists it will resume talks if they begin where the last round left off.
Moratinos' trip to Egypt was his second since he was named the EU envoy to the Middle East to boost Europe's role in the U.S.-dominated peace negotiations in the region.

Last week the chairman of the EU council of ministers, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, said in Cairo that the EU was seeking a greater role in the Middle East peace process, especially by helping Syria and Israel to resume peace talks.
He said Moratinos was prepared to visit Assad.
Moratinos said that he was leaving Cairo on Sunday going to Cyprus, and would return to Israel on Monday to discuss the results of his visit with members of the Israeli government.
